inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL cash-flow add-back (ShareBasedCompensation) TTM to 2026-06-30 = 268; plus kpis.equity_award_taxes (taxes paid on net-share settlement, financing) TTM = 101. ICE publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure (its non-GAAP adjustments exclude acquisition amortization, not SBC), so the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM repurchases FY2025 1,294 + H1-26 1,202 - H1-25 496 = 2,000. ICE is an active repurchaser, so the flat diluted count is funded, not a convention; buybacks are value-neutral here because SBC is fully expensed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Basic shares 566m at 2026-06-30 (XBRL) plus ~2m dilutive RSU/PSU awards from the 10-Q EPS note = 568m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). No non-SBC issuance is planned: MarketAxess is an all-cash deal.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 gives cost of equity ~9.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% on $19.8bn of senior notes (~3.6% after tax); equity ~$87bn vs debt ~$20bn (rising to ~$25bn post-MarketAxess) gives D/V ~20%. WACC = 0.80 x 9.2 + 0.20 x 3.6 = 8.1%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; scenario risk is carried by the driver paths and weights, not by a per-scenario discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial for ICE (~$300m of lease liabilities against $19.8bn of debt); lease cost is left inside EBITDA as an operating expense and lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests (~$40m, mainly the ICE Futures Europe / NYSE consolidated subsidiaries) are immaterial; flows are consolidated and no NCI deduction is made in the bridge.
inputs.revenue_basis_note: base_revenue is GROSS GAAP revenue as carried in ICE_Metrics.csv (includes ~$2.6-3.3bn/yr of pass-through transaction-based expenses: Section 31 fees, cash-equity liquidity payments, routing). All margin paths are therefore on the gross basis: 52% GAAP EBITDA on gross revenue corresponds to ~65-70% on management's net-revenue basis. Dollar EBITDA is what the model capitalises, so the basis is a presentation choice made to stay consistent with the CSV history.
inputs.marketaxess_note: The $5.7bn EV / $167-per-share cash acquisition of MarketAxess (announced 2026-07-29, expected close H1 2027) is NOT modelled. It is funded with ~$3.5-3.75bn of senior notes plus a $2bn delayed-draw term loan, both post-dating the 2026-06-30 balance sheet; until close the notes sit as cash and debt equally, so net debt is unchanged. At ~14x MarketAxess EBITDA against ICE's own ~15x, and with the 33% premium (~$1.5bn) roughly offset by the capitalised value of the $100m run-rate synergies, the deal is close to value-neutral to ICE holders and is left as an unmodelled bridge item. On completion the model should add MarketAxess revenue/EBITDA to the base and the ~$5.7bn to net debt.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: operating company). ICE is an exchange/clearing/data/mortgage-software operator whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; it is not a bank (clearing-margin deposits are segregated pass-through balances, not deposits funding a lending book), so residual-income is wrong, and it is a repurchaser of its own stock, so BVPS compounding is wrong. FY0 is the TTM to Jun-2026, which embeds a record derivatives-volume year (H1-26 gross revenue +12%, net income +44%): the base path therefore starts with year-1 growth of 4% (recurring +7-8% on ~60% of revenue, transaction revenue mean-reverting) rather than the trailing 9% CAGR, and the bear path starts at 0%. The trailing CAGRs also include the Sep-2023 Black Knight acquisition, so they overstate organic growth by ~2-3pp. D&A includes ~$700m/yr of acquisition-intangible amortisation (Black Knight, Ellie Mae) that runs off; da_pct declines from 11.5% to 9.5% and the cash-tax rate of 25% (FY2025 cash taxes 1,100 on ~4,400 pre-tax, above the ~23% book rate because that amortisation is largely non-deductible) is held. Owner FCF (levered, TTM) is 4,709; the engine's unlevered year-1 owner FCF should come out near 5,200-5,300, the difference being ~$600m of after-tax interest that the WACC carries instead. Cap multiple 20x owner FCF; ICE's own EV/unlevered-owner-FCF today is ~21x, so no multiple expansion is assumed. No interest income stripped (net debt $18.8bn, no net cash). Euroclear stake (~9.8%, ~$0.7bn at cost) and other equity investments are left out of the bridge as a conservative omission (~$1/share).

historical_growth.notes: CAGRs FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) on annual gross revenue, diluted EPS, shareholders' equity and owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award taxes; no interest income to strip). The 3yr EPS CAGR of 30.8% is off a FY2022 base depressed by Bakkt/investment losses (EPS 2.59) and is not a growth signal; the 5yr figure of 8.8% is the honest read. Owner-FCF CAGRs (8.4%/9.9%) sit within 0.4pp of reported FCF CAGRs: SBC is ~2.7% of revenue and has grown in line with the business, not faster. All series include the Sep-2023 Black Knight acquisition (~$1bn+ of acquired revenue, debt-funded), so organic growth is ~2-3pp lower than these figures; the projected base path starts at 4-5.5%, not 8%.

base.narrative: Recurring revenue (~60%) compounds at 6-8% per the raised FY2026 guidance; transaction revenue gives back part of the 2026 volume boom in year 1 then grows with the cycle; mortgage tech recovers gradually. Blended gross-revenue growth 4% -> 5.5% -> fading to 3%. EBITDA margin drifts up 180bp over ten years on Black Knight synergies and data-business operating leverage. D&A falls as acquisition amortisation runs off; cash tax held at 25%; SBC ~2.7% of revenue.

bull.narrative: Derivatives volumes stay elevated (rates and energy volatility persist), a multi-year US mortgage-origination recovery lifts Mortgage Technology to double-digit growth, FIDS recurring revenue holds at 8%+ and the fixed-income electronification thesis (MarketAxess, not modelled, would add to this) plays out. Operating leverage on data and mortgage tech takes gross-basis EBITDA margin to 57%.

bear.narrative: The 2026 volume peak reverses: a low-volatility regime cuts transaction revenue ~10% (year-1 growth 0% despite recurring growth), prediction-market platforms (Kalshi, Polymarket) take fee share and force pricing concessions in event/adjacent contracts, the mortgage recovery stalls on a rate reversal, and the MarketAxess integration distracts at 3x+ leverage. Negative operating leverage takes gross-basis margin down ~280bp; the terminal cap is cut to 16x for a slower, more leveraged franchise.

scenario_narratives.base: ICE compounds as a diversified financial-infrastructure operator: ~60% recurring revenue (data, connectivity, listings, mortgage SaaS) growing 6-8%, transaction revenue mean-reverting from the record 2026 derivatives year and then growing with the cycle, and Mortgage Technology recovering slowly as affordability improves. Gross-revenue growth of 4% in year 1 rising to 5.5% and fading to 3%; EBITDA margin (gross basis) 52% -> 54% on Black Knight synergies and data operating leverage; acquisition amortisation runs off; cash tax 25%; SBC ~2.7% of revenue; 20x terminal cap not binding (Gordon at 2.5% binds).
scenario_narratives.bull: Volatility stays high across rates and energy, the US mortgage cycle turns decisively (origination tech +10%, closing solutions +20% already in H1-26), FIDS recurring revenue sustains 8%+, and fixed-income electronification (MarketAxess) adds a growth leg. Growth 6-8% for five years, margin to 57%, terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The volume boom unwinds into a calm-market regime, prediction-market entrants erode derivatives economics, the mortgage recovery stalls on higher rates, and leverage (~3x post-MarketAxess) plus the FTC prior-approval order leave no room for offsetting M&A. Growth 0-3%, margin compresses to 49.5%, 16x cap, terminal growth 2%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 20% because ICE is stacking a second debt-funded acquisition (MarketAxess) on the Black Knight balance sheet at ~2.8-3x adjusted EBITDA while FY0 is a record-volume year, so downside from a volume mean-reversion and integration slip is more than tail risk; there is no going-concern or covenant risk, which is why it is not 25-30%. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: sustained volatility, a US housing/mortgage recovery and the fixed-income electronification thesis. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value ICE as a stream of unlevered owner free cash flow, built from components (gross revenue -> GAAP EBITDA -> SBC incl. withholding -> D&A -> 25% cash tax -> capex incl. capitalised software) over a 10-year horizon, discounted at an 8% USD WACC, with net debt of $18.8bn deducted and a flat 568m diluted share count. SBC is charged once, in the flows. The record FY2026 volume year is the base, so year-1 growth is deliberately below trend and the bear case starts at zero growth. MarketAxess is treated as value-neutral and left outside the model until close.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY0 embeds a record derivatives-volume year; if transaction revenue reverts harder than the 4%/0% year-1 paths assume, base and bear values fall together
Terminal value is ~60% of EV: each 50bp on WACC or terminal growth moves value ~8-10%
Net debt rises by ~$5.7bn on MarketAxess close (H1 2027); if synergies or MarketAxess growth disappoint, the unmodelled deal becomes value-destructive rather than neutral
Gross-revenue basis: a rise in pass-through Section 31 fees inflates revenue growth without adding EBITDA, so margin on this basis can drift down for non-economic reasons
Prediction-market/event-contract regulation could reprice the derivatives-exchange franchise faster than a bear margin path captures
The 25% cash tax rate rests on FY2025 cash taxes; a change in the deductibility of acquisition amortisation or in US corporate tax policy moves NOPAT directly
